testCases.input: My name is Anjali and I am studying the LLM evals course. What is the difference between model evals and application evals?
testCases.actualOutput:
Hello Anjali! It's great to see your interest in understanding the differences between model evals and application evals in the context of LLM evaluations. 

To start, model evals and application evals serve distinct purposes in the evaluation process. Model evals are focused on assessing the capabilities of the language models themselves. This means that when a new LLM is released, model evals are used to test and benchmark its performance against various standards or benchmarks. The goal here is to document how well the model performs, often resulting in metrics that indicate its accuracy and effectiveness on specific tasks.

On the other hand, application evals are concerned with evaluating LLM-based applications. This involves assessing how well these applications perform in real-world scenarios and whether they meet user needs. Essentially, application evals help determine if an LLM-powered application is functioning effectively and is ready for users.

In summary, the key difference lies in their focus: model evals evaluate the language models themselves, while application evals assess the applications that utilize these models. Understanding this distinction is crucial as it helps clarify the context in which each type of evaluation is applied. If you have any more questions or need further clarification, feel free to ask!
